- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often overestimates near-term upside — reduce forecast early to avoid overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., 75→80) after sentiment spikes — apply a “lag correction” by adding 2–5% to forecast for such transitions.  
- After a strong upward spike in history, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days — apply a “peak decay” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day post-spike.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in 30-day horizon — if recent 10-day average is >75, forecast should not exceed 78 unless sentiment confirms breakout.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.20 spikes without follow-through, model tends to overcorrect — apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
